article.title: Granite Switch 4.1.1 — Update models like you update software

harvestedTerms.summary: IBM Granite Switch 4.1.1 patch release introduces a modular adapter architecture for language models, framed explicitly as software-style versioning. The article highlights a Speech ASR update and a Decision adapter improvement, emphasising that only the changed adapters are retrained — the base model is untouched. An Adapter SDK is promised for third-party developers.

article.title: An Interview with Palantir CTO Shyam Sankar About the AI Religious War

harvestedTerms.summary: A Stratechery interview with Palantir CTO Shyam Sankar covering AI diffusion, systems engineering approaches to AI safety, forward-deployed engineering, the 'AI religious war' framing, and Palantir's lessons from AI adoption. Rich in geopolitical-industrial framing and contrarian perspectives on how AI value is actually created and captured.

longlistAdditions.label: Systems Engineering Approach to AI Safety

mustReadFlagged.reason: A rare extended interview with a senior Palantir executive who offers a genuinely distinct perspective on AI adoption — focused on diffusion over capability, systems engineering over alignment philosophy, and alpha-capture over productivity gains. Worth reading for the contrarian framing and the practitioner critique of how labs approach safety.

article.title: Building a multiplayer game world with autonomous Fable-class models

harvestedTerms.summary: Simon Willison links to a Jacob Sansbury post describing Spawn, a multiplayer game built and continuously deployed by a swarm of autonomous Fable-class agents at ~$3M/month in token spend. The piece is a live case study in extreme agentic engineering: agents read their own error logs, file their own bugs, ship to production hourly, and treat an hour without a ship as a SEV-0 incident. The article also documents model-switching experiments (Fable 5.1 vs Opus 5.5 vs GPT-6 Astra) revealing sharp differences in autonomous reliability at this task scope.

mustReadFlagged.reason: A rare primary source on what fully autonomous, production-grade agentic engineering actually looks like at scale: agents that file their own bugs, read their own logs, and ship hourly under a norm where not shipping is the emergency. The model-comparison vignette (Fable 5.1 vs. Opus 5.5 vs. GPT-6 Astra's security-review fiasco) is the kind of empirical detail that sharpens thinking about autonomous reliability in ways that benchmarks don't.

article.title: You can generate and edit Google Docs files directly in Gemini chats now

harvestedTerms.summary: Google Gemini now supports generating and editing Google Docs, Sheets, slide decks, PDFs, Markdown, TXT files, and code directly within the chat interface — without leaving the app. The feature is live for all Gemini users, with PDF editing on web and mobile and other formats web-only. This mirrors a similar capability Anthropic launched in Claude chats earlier this year.
